value.body: KYC (know your customer) and AML (anti-money laundering) analysts check that a bank's or financial firm's customers are who they say they are, and look for signs of money laundering or fraud. They work at banks, NBFCs, fintechs, brokerages and service centres doing this work for global banks. Most days involve reviewing documents and alerts and recording a decision.

items.label: Rules that apply
items.value: PMLA, 2002 and RBI's KYC Master Direction
items.note: Domestic roles; global-bank roles follow those banks' home rules

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Case management systems, screening tools, Excel

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Banks and service centres hire graduates in batches and train them on their own procedures. Short certifications in AML (for example from industry bodies) and good written English help at interviews.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Document review and attention to detail

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is process-driven and often measured on volume and accuracy.
Common next steps: senior analyst, quality reviewer, or financial crime investigations.
Shift work is common in roles serving overseas banks.
